text:
Maya Gomez: Hey all, first day here! Followed the onboarding guide but my kubeconfig only has a "default" context. Need to get access to a personal dev ns (maya-dev). Who should I ping?

Ravi Singh: welcome Maya :tada: Are you on Okta SSO and device enrolled? If yes, try `redwood-sso login --okta` and then `kubectl config get-contexts`.

Maya Gomez: I did the SSO and enrolled. `kubectl config get-contexts` shows only `default`. `kubectl config view --raw` contexts block shows cluster: redwood-dev but user line is `maya@redwood.ai` (not okta prefixed).

Ravi Singh: that explains it. Our Okta connector writes an exec plugin user like `okta:maya@redwood.ai`. @infra-ops can you trigger a directory sync and create namespace `maya-dev` + rolebinding once Maya is mapped?

infra-ops: queued a directory sync for maya@redwood.ai (job id sync-2026-08-12-07). Will create ns/rb after mapping confirmed.

Maya Gomez: after sync I re-ran `redwood-sso login` and now `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n maya-dev` -> "no" (expected).

infra-ops: created namespace `maya-dev` and rolebinding `rb-maya-dev-edit` granting `edit` to `okta:maya@redwood.ai`. Applied.

Maya Gomez: `kubectl get pods -n maya-dev` -> "no resources found". I can list! Set context default ns and port-forward works. Thanks folks :raised_hands:

Ravi Singh: added a note to the onboarding doc about the common symptom (user not prefixed with okta) and to run `redwood-sso doctor` if `kubectl` errors after SSO. Welcome again!
